entities.name: PMID:25082847
observations: Cardiovascular Research 2014 study directly compared ex-vivo EPO-primed versus unprimed G-CSF-mobilized human PBMCs.
Healthy donors received G-CSF 10 μg/kg subcutaneously for 3 days; cells were primed with EPO 10 IU/mL for 6 hours.
The study reported enhanced vasculogenic activity in vitro and in Matrigel plug, ischemic hindlimb, and myocardial-infarction mouse models, but accessible results lacked numerical effect sizes.

entities.name: Erythropoietin
observations: Ex-vivo priming at 10 IU/mL for 6 hours was associated with increased vasculogenic-factor and integrin expression in G-CSF-mobilized human PBMCs.

entities.name: G-CSF-mobilized human PBMCs
observations: Human PBMCs mobilized by 3 days of G-CSF were the cellular substrate for EPO priming and vasculogenic assays.

entities.name: EPO priming improves PBMC vasculogenesis
observations: EPO priming increased IL-8, IL-10, bFGF, PDGF, MMP9 and integrins αV, β1, β2, β8, enhanced endothelial migration and tube formation via conditioned medium, and increased adhesion to endothelial cells or fibronectin.

EPO-primed cells showed augmented activity in Matrigel plug, ischemic hindlimb, and myocardial-infarction models, with reported incorporation into mouse vasculature and humoral effects from cell supernatant.
The direction of effect was favorable, but accessible evidence did not report numerical effect sizes, sample sizes, or P values.
